info.title: Instaclustr API Documentation
info.description:
Welcome to the Instaclustr API Documentation. This page shows the current endpoints that are supported by Instaclustr. For more information on how to use the Instaclustr platform, refer to our documentation. If you have any questions or need assistance, please feel free to reach out to us anytime at support@instaclustr.com. # Usage Instructions

Rate Limits

Requests to endpoints are rate limited. Exceeding this limit will return a 429 error code until that user’s request threshold falls below this limit. To find the Rate Limits relevant to the endpoint, refer to the Authentication & Rate Limit section for the endpoint. For more information, see Rate Limit Documentation.

tags.name: Service User Management API
tags.description:
Operations related to service user management.
Service Users are API-only users. Service Users are created in, and have access to, a single account. This account is the account associated with the API key that was used to create the Service User via the API. Owner and Cluster Admin level users in an account can create Service Users. The user who creates a Service User automatically becomes an Administrator of that Service User. Administrators of a Service User may invite additional Cluster Admin users to be Controllers of that user. Owner users in an account automatically have Administrator-level access to all Service Users in that account.
A Service User may not have multiple API keys of the same type, however an account can create multiple Service Users.

tags.name: Cluster Management V2 - Trait
tags.description:
Operations related to managing clusters.

Authentication - These requests require either a Provisioning API Key or Read Only Provisioning API Key. The Provisioning API Key has full access to all endpoints listed in this category while the Read Only Provision API Key can only perform GET requests to endpoints.
Account API keys can be retrieved any time from the console by going to gear icon to the top right > Account Settings > API Keys.

Rate Limit - Requests to the Cluster Management V2 are rate limited. Exceeding this rate will return a 429 error code until that user’s request threshold falls below this limit. For more information, see Rate Limit Documentation.

tags.name: Monitoring - Trait
tags.description:
Operations related to monitoring clusters, data centres and nodes. Authentication - These requests require the Monitoring API Key.
Account API keys can be retrieved any time from the console by going to gear icon to the top right > Account Settings > API Keys.

Rate Limit - Requests to the Monitoring are rate limited. Exceeding this rate will return a 429 error code until that user’s request threshold falls below this limit. For more information, see Rate Limit Documentation.

tags.name: User Management and SCIM 2.0 API - Trait
tags.description:
Operations related to user management. Several operations implement the SCIM 2.0 protocol.

Authentication - These requests require the User Management API Key. Moreover, User Management and SCIM 2.0 API requests require a key generated by an Account Owner user. Account API keys can be retrieved any time from the console by going to gear icon to the top right > Account Settings > API Keys.

Rate Limit - Requests to the User Management endpoints are rate limited to 750 requests per minute. Exceeding this rate will return a 429 error code until that user’s request threshold falls below this limit. For more information, see Rate Limit Documentation.

get.summary: Get raw AWS CloudFormation template for Bring-Your-Own-Cloud (BYOC) setup.
get.description: Returns the raw AWS CloudFormation template for BYOC setup as a JSON string. When `bucketName` and/or `iamRoleName` are supplied, the corresponding `@@S3_BACKUP_BUCKET_NAME@@` / `@@IAM_ROLE_NAME@@` placeholders are substituted with those values; otherwise they are left as placeholders for the customer to fill in.

parameters.name: bucketName
parameters.description: The customer's S3 backup bucket name to substitute for the `@@S3_BACKUP_BUCKET_NAME@@` placeholder. If omitted, the placeholder is left unsubstituted.

parameters.name: iamRoleName
parameters.description: The customer's IAM role name to substitute for the `@@IAM_ROLE_NAME@@` placeholder. If omitted, the placeholder is left unsubstituted.

parameters.name: cloudProviderAccountId
parameters.description: The customer's AWS account ID. When supplied together with `dataCentre`, used to set the CloudFormation `CreateKeyPair` parameter default to `false` if another RUNNING BYOC setup already exists for the same AWS account and data centre region under this Instaclustr account; otherwise defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: dataCentre
parameters.description: The AWS data centre region for this BYOC setup (e.g. `US_EAST_1`). Must be supplied together with `cloudProviderAccountId` to determine the `CreateKeyPair` default.

200.description: Successfully retrieved raw AWS CloudFormation template for BYOC setup as a JSON string.

get.summary: Download raw AWS CloudFormation template as a JSON file for Bring-Your-Own-Cloud (BYOC) setup.
get.description: Returns the AWS CloudFormation template for BYOC setup as a downloadable .json file. When `bucketName` and/or `iamRoleName` are supplied, the corresponding `@@S3_BACKUP_BUCKET_NAME@@` / `@@IAM_ROLE_NAME@@` placeholders are substituted with those values; otherwise they are left as placeholders for the customer to fill in.

parameters.name: bucketName
parameters.description: The customer's S3 backup bucket name to substitute for the `@@S3_BACKUP_BUCKET_NAME@@` placeholder. If omitted, the placeholder is left unsubstituted.

parameters.name: iamRoleName
parameters.description: The customer's IAM role name to substitute for the `@@IAM_ROLE_NAME@@` placeholder. If omitted, the placeholder is left unsubstituted.

parameters.name: cloudProviderAccountId
parameters.description: The customer's AWS account ID. When supplied together with `dataCentre`, used to set the CloudFormation `CreateKeyPair` parameter default to `false` if another RUNNING BYOC setup already exists for the same AWS account and data centre region under this Instaclustr account; otherwise defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: dataCentre
parameters.description: The AWS data centre region for this BYOC setup (e.g. `US_EAST_1`). Must be supplied together with `cloudProviderAccountId` to determine the `CreateKeyPair` default.

200.description: Successfully retrieved raw AWS CloudFormation template for BYOC setup as a JSON file.

get.summary: Download raw AWS Terraform templates as a ZIP archive for Bring-Your-Own-Cloud (BYOC) setup.
get.description: Returns an AWS Terraform template for BYOC setup as a downloadable ZIP archive. When setup parameters are supplied, the corresponding Terraform variable defaults are populated and the template is tailored for an initial setup or an additional region. When omitted, the original raw template with placeholders is returned for backwards compatibility.

parameters.name: bucketName
parameters.description: The S3 backup bucket name to use as the Terraform `bucket_name` default.

parameters.name: iamRoleName
parameters.description: The existing or new IAM role name to use as the Terraform `iam_role_name` default.

parameters.name: cloudProviderAccountId
parameters.description: The customer's AWS account ID. Must be supplied together with `dataCentre` to determine whether the regional template should create the IAM role and EC2 key pair.

parameters.name: dataCentre
parameters.description: The AWS Data Centre Region for the template (for example, `US_EAST_1`). Must be supplied together with `cloudProviderAccountId`.

200.description: Successfully retrieved raw AWS Terraform templates for BYOC setup as a ZIP archive.

get.summary: Get Active Cluster IDs, result can be optionally filtered on conditions specified by query parameter
get.description: Get Active Cluster IDs, result can be optionally filtered on conditions specified by query parameter

parameters.name: search
parameters.description:
- Simple search mode: searches for clusters that have any field of {`name`, `id`, `description`} which contains search string.
 - Advanced search mode: String of space separated *key:value* entries where `key` is from {*name*, *id*, *desc*, *app*, *tag*} and `value` is the actual string value to search for. 
    - There can be single occurrence of *name*, *id*, *desc*, *app* key and their value are matched by string inclusion check, case insensitive.
     - For *tag* key, there can be multiple entries and their search values should be of format *tagKey:tagValue*, match is determined when cluster contains a tag with exact `tagKey` case sensitively, and the tag value contains `tagValue` case insensitively.
 - Example: 
    - `search=name:str1 id:str2 desc:str3 app:APACHE_CASSANDRA tag:env:prod tag:managed_by:tf`
    - `search=someClusterName`

200.description: Retrieved Cluster IDs.

get.summary: Retrieve monitoring metrics
get.description:
Metrics definitions for single or all nodes in a cluster or cluster data center.The set of available metrics will expand with changes to the monitoring API.

The possible values for the metrics parameter is listed below:

General Metrics
  • n::cpuUtilization Current CPU utilisation as a percentage of total available.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_utilization
  • n::osload Current OS load.
    • Available sub-types:
      • last_one_minute Average metric value over 1 minute.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
      • last_five_minutes Average metric value over 5 minutes.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload

Kafka Broker Level Per-Topic Metrics

Per-topic metric names follow the format kt::{topic}::{metricName}. Optionally, a ‘sub-type’ may be specified to return a specific part of the metric - kt::{topic}::{metricName}:{subType}

  • kt::{topic}::messagesInPerTopic The rate of messages received by the topic. One sub-type must be specified.
    JMX Collection Path: type=BrokerTopicMetrics,name=MessagesInPerSec,topic=%s

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

get.summary: Kafka - Retrieve consumer group client metrics
get.description:
All metrics are reported under a consumer group and the consumed topic aggregated at a client level. A client within a consumer group is a logical grouping defined by setting the client.id configuration on a consumer. Available Metrics:
  • consumerLag : defined as the sum of consumer lag reported by all consumers with the same client id.
  • partitionCount : defined as the total number of partitions assigned to consumers with the same client id.
  • consumerCount : defined as the total number of consumers with the same client id.

get.summary: Kafka - Retrieve topic level metrics for all topics
get.description:
To request the same metrics for all topics, do not define the topic in the path. If the number of metrics retrieved by the query exceeds 20, the endpoint will paginate through the topics using the query parameter of pageNumber. Available Metrics:
  • topicMessageDistribution : Metrics derived by analysing the message distribution among partitions of a topic. Metrics will be reported for non internal topics only.
    • outliers : Number of partitions identified as outliers using the statistical method of MADe (reference). With the high and low fences defined by (median ± 2 * 1.4826 * MAD). The metric will also return a JSON array of outlier partitions and their message counts. This metric will be limited to periods of 1h or below for retrieval.
    • standard_deviation : the population standard deviation of message distribution across partitions for the topic

parameters.name: clusterId
parameters.description: Target cluster ID.

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

schema.description:
• If set to DEFAULT, response will be returned in JSON format.
  • If set to PROMETHEUS, text response will be returned in Prometheus format.
  • If not provided, response will be returned in default format, i.e. JSON.

200.description: Successfully retrieved topic level metrics for all topics.

Prometheus response ('format' query para.description: Prometheus response ('format' query parameter specified as 'prometheus')
Prometheus response ('format' query para.value:
# HELP kafka_topic_message_distribution Data type: outliers, Unit: 1
# TYPE kafka_topic_message_distribution gauge
kafka_topic_message_distribution{topic="instaclustr-sla",type="outliers",} 2.0
# HELP kafka_topic_message_distribution Data type: standard_deviation, Unit: 1
# TYPE kafka_topic_message_distribution gauge
kafka_topic_message_distribution{topic="instaclustr-sla",type="standard_deviation",} 5.23

get.summary: Retrieve paged monitoring metrics
get.description:
Metrics information is provided with either for an individual node or for all nodes in a cluster and cluster data centre. The number of results displayed will depend on the startIndex and count parameter. For Kafka broker level topic metrics, this paged metrics also accepts wildcard character * in the place of unknown topics. The set of available metrics will expand as we build out this API.

The possible values for the metrics parameter is listed below:

General Metrics
  • n::cpuUtilization Current CPU utilisation as a percentage of total available.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_utilization
  • n::osload Current OS load.
    • Available sub-types:
      • last_one_minute Average metric value over 1 minute.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
      • last_five_minutes Average metric value over 5 minutes.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
      • last_fifteen_minutes Average metric value over 15 minutes.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
  • n::diskUtilization Total disk space utilisation as a percentage of total available.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_utilization
  • n::diskAvailable Disk space available in bytes
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_available
  • n::diskUsed Disk space used in bytes
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_used
  • n::diskReadOps Read operations per second on the data disk
    • Sub-type: count_per_second Per second rate, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.
      Unit: units per second (1/s)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_read_ops_per_second
  • n::diskWriteOps Write operations per second on the data disk
    • Sub-type: count_per_second Per second rate, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.
      Unit: units per second (1/s)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_write_ops_per_second
  • n::diskRead Cumulative bytes read from the data disk since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: bytes_total Cumulative total bytes
      Unit: bytes (B)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_read_bytes_total
  • n::diskWrite Cumulative bytes written to the data disk since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: bytes_total Cumulative total bytes
      Unit: bytes (B)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_write_bytes_total
  • n::diskReadLatency Average read latency in milliseconds per operation on the data disk
    • Sub-type: ms
      Unit: milliseconds (ms)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_read_latency_milliseconds
  • n::diskWriteLatency Average write latency in milliseconds per operation on the data disk
    • Sub-type: ms
      Unit: milliseconds (ms)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_write_latency_milliseconds
  • n::diskIoUtilization Percentage of the 20 second sampling interval the data disk spent servicing I/O requests.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_io_utilization
  • n::diskIoTimeWeighted Cumulative weighted I/O time in milliseconds for the data disk since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total milliseconds
      Unit: milliseconds (ms)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_io_time_weighted_milliseconds_total
  • n::cpuguestpercent Time spent running a virtual CPU for guest OS under control of kernel.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpuguestpercent
  • n::cpuguestnicepercent Niced processes executing in user mode in virtual OS.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpuguestnicepercent
  • n::cpusystempercent Percentage of processes executing in kernel mode.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpusystempercent
  • n::cpuidlepercent Percentage of time when one or more kernel threads are executing with the run queue empty and/or no I/O operations are currently cycling.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpuidlepercent
  • n::cpuiowaitpercent CPU time the I/O thread spent waiting for a socket ready for reads or writes as a percent.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpuiowaitpercent
  • n::cpuirqpercent Number of hardware interrupts the kernel is servicing.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpuirqpercent
  • n::cpunicepercent Percentage of processes executing in user mode which have a positive nice value.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpunicepercent
  • n::cpusoftirqpercent Number of software interrupts the kernel is servicing.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpusoftirqpercent
  • n::cpustealpercent Percentage of time the hypervisor allocated to other tasks external to the one run on the current virtual CPU
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpustealpercent
  • n::cpuuserpercent Processes executing in user mode, including application processes.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpuuserpercent
  • n::memavailable Estimate of how much memory is available to start new applications without swap, taking into account page cache and re-claimability of slab.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_memavailable
  • n::networkindelta Delta count of bytes received over a 20-second sampling window.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkindelta
  • n::networkoutdelta Delta count of bytes transmitted over a 20-second sampling window.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkoutdelta
  • n::networkin Bytes received per second on the primary network interface, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkin
  • n::networkout Bytes transmitted per second on the primary network interface, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkout
  • n::networkinerrorsdelta Delta count of receive errors detected.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkinerrorsdelta
  • n::networkouterrorsdelta Delta count of transmit packets dropped.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkouterrorsdelta
  • n::networkindroppeddelta Delta count of receive packets dropped.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkindroppeddelta
  • n::networkoutdroppeddelta Delta count of transmit packets dropped.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkoutdroppeddelta
  • n::networkinBytes Cumulative bytes received on the primary network interface since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: bytes_total Cumulative total bytes
      Unit: bytes (B)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkin_bytes_total
  • n::networkoutBytes Cumulative bytes transmitted on the primary network interface since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: bytes_total Cumulative total bytes
      Unit: bytes (B)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_networkout_bytes_total
  • n::cpuTaskRuntime Cumulative nanoseconds all tasks have spent running on CPU across all cores since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total nanoseconds
      Unit: nanoseconds (ns)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_task_runtime_nanoseconds_total
  • n::cpuTaskWaitTime Cumulative nanoseconds all tasks have spent waiting in the CPU run queue across all cores since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total nanoseconds
      Unit: nanoseconds (ns)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_task_wait_time_nanoseconds_total
  • n::cpuTimeSlices Cumulative number of CPU timeslices run across all cores since boot
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total of the metric.
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_time_slices_total
  • n::cpuPressureSome Cumulative microseconds of time at least one task was stalled waiting for CPU, since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total microseconds
      Unit: microseconds (us)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_pressure_some_microseconds_total
  • n::ioPressureSome Cumulative microseconds of time at least one task was stalled waiting for I/O, since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total microseconds
      Unit: microseconds (us)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_io_pressure_some_microseconds_total
  • n::ioPressureFull Cumulative microseconds of time all tasks were simultaneously stalled on I/O, since boot. A monotonically-increasing counter
    • Sub-type: total Cumulative total microseconds
      Unit: microseconds (us)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_io_pressure_full_microseconds_total
  • n::filedescriptorlimit Maximum number of open files limit for the node OS.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_filedescriptorlimit
  • n::filedescriptoropencount Current number of open files in the node OS.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_filedescriptoropencount
  • n::tcpestablished Number of open TCP connections.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_tcpestablished
  • n::tcptimewait Number of TCP sockets waiting for enough time to pass to be sure the remote TCP received the acknowledgment of its connection termination request.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_tcptimewait
  • n::tcplistening Number of TCP sockets waiting for a connection request from any remote TCP and port.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_tcplistening
  • n::tcpall Total number of TCP connections in all state.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_tcpall
  • n::tcpclosewait Number of TCP sockets which connection is in the process of being closed.
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_tcpclosewait

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

schema.description:
• If set to DEFAULT, response will be returned in JSON format.
  • If set to PROMETHEUS, text response will be returned in Prometheus format.
  • If not provided, response will be returned in default format, i.e. JSON.

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

schema.description:
• If set to DEFAULT, response will be returned in JSON format.
  • If set to PROMETHEUS, text response will be returned in Prometheus format.

get.summary: Retrieve paged monitoring metrics
get.description:
Metrics information is provided with either for an individual node or for all nodes in a cluster and cluster data centre. The number of results displayed will depend on the startIndex and count parameter. For Kafka broker level topic metrics, this paged metrics also accepts wildcard character * in the place of unknown topics. The set of available metrics will expand as we build out this API.

The possible values for the metrics parameter is listed below:

    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_utilization

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

schema.description:
• If set to DEFAULT, response will be returned in JSON format.
  • If set to PROMETHEUS, text response will be returned in Prometheus format.
  • If not provided, response will be returned in default format, i.e. JSON.

get.summary: Retrieve monitoring metrics
get.description:
Metrics definitions for single or all nodes in a cluster or cluster data center.The set of available metrics will expand with changes to the monitoring API.

The possible values for the metrics parameter is listed below:

  • n::diskReadOps Read operations per second on the data disk
    • Sub-type: count_per_second Per second rate, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.
      Unit: units per second (1/s)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_read_ops_per_second
  • n::diskWriteOps Write operations per second on the data disk

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

get.summary: Retrieve paged monitoring metrics
get.description:
Metrics information is provided with either for an individual node or for all nodes in a cluster and cluster data centre. The number of results displayed will depend on the startIndex and count parameter. For Kafka broker level topic metrics, this paged metrics also accepts wildcard character * in the place of unknown topics. The set of available metrics will expand as we build out this API.

The possible values for the metrics parameter is listed below:

General Metrics
  • n::cpuUtilization Current CPU utilisation as a percentage of total available.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_cpu_utilization
  • n::osload Current OS load.
    • Available sub-types:
      • last_one_minute Average metric value over 1 minute.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
      • last_five_minutes Average metric value over 5 minutes.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
      • last_fifteen_minutes Average metric value over 15 minutes.
        Prometheus Name: ic_node_osload
  • n::diskUtilization Total disk space utilisation as a percentage of total available.
    • Sub-type: percentage
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_utilization
  • n::diskAvailable Disk space available in bytes
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_available
  • n::diskUsed Disk space used in bytes
    • Sub-type: value
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_used
  • n::diskReadOps Read operations per second on the data disk
    • Sub-type: count_per_second Per second rate, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.
      Unit: units per second (1/s)
      Prometheus Name: ic_node_disk_read_ops_per_second
  • n::diskWriteOps Write operations per second on the data disk
    • Sub-type: count_per_second Per second rate, averaged over a 20-second sampling window.

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: The metrics to return are specified as a comma-delimited query string parameter. Up to 20 metrics may be specified.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description:
The period of time from which monitoring information is returned. It is also assigned a period type. Formatted as: period=\&type=\.
Allowable values: 1m, 15m, 1h, 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The type of metrics value extracted from metrics values for a period of time.
  • If specified as 'latest', then the latest metric will be returned regardless what 'period' query parameter is set.
  • If specified as 'aggregate', then the metric value returned will be the average of all metric values from the specific period to now.
  • If specified as 'range', then the metric values returned will be the series of all metric values from the specific period to end.

parameters.name: reportNaN
parameters.description: If a metric value is NaN or null, reportNaN determines whether API should report it as NaN. The default behaviour is false and NaN and null will be reported as 0. Setting reportNaN=true will return NaN values in the API response.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify the end time for the retrieved metric values. For example, if you set this to a timestamp which is 10 minutes prior to the current time, the metric values returned will be for that point of time. Please note that the format is milliseconds since Epoch.

schema.description:
• If set to DEFAULT, response will be returned in JSON format.
  • If set to PROMETHEUS, text response will be returned in Prometheus format.
  • If not provided, response will be returned in default format, i.e. JSON.

Per-topic metric names follow the format kt::{topic}::{metricName}. Optionally, a ‘sub-type’ may be specified to return a specific part of the metric - kt::{topic}::{metricName}:{subType}

  • kt::{topic}::messagesInPerTopic The rate of messages received by the topic. One sub-type must be specified.
    JMX Collection Path: type=BrokerTopicMetrics,name=MessagesInPerSec,topic=%s
    • Available sub-types:
      • one_minute_rate One minute rate of the measured metric.
        Prometheus Name: ic_topic_messages_in_per_topic

patch.description: Patch an Instaclustr user provisioned through SCIM by the given User Management API key. Deactivating a user will unlink it from all SCIM groups, accounts and organizations, and will exclude the user from all SCIM user queries. It is not possible to activate a user who is an OWNER of a SCIM group. For non-PCI account, the targeting deactivation user must not be the last owner for any of the linked accounts. For PCI account or for accounts with Inactivity Settings enabled, the targeting deactivation user must not be the second last owner for any of the linked accounts. Deactivating a user will completely deactivate the user from Instaclustr, preventing it from logging in to Instaclustr console and API, and access to any accounts and organizations. Activating a user will include the user in all SCIM user queries. An Instaclustr user cannot be deleted via SCIM. To permanently delete an Instaclustr user contact support@instaclustr.com. Note - While the request accepts all properties compliant with the SCIM 2.0 protocol, properties not listed in the request body schema will be ignored for the operation.

providerAccountName.description: Name of the provider account.

iamRoleName.description: Custom IAM role name for BYOC setup. If not provided, defaults to 'instaclustr-<account-id>'. Must be 1-64 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters and +=,.@-_ symbols.

skipKeyPairCreation.description: When true, an EC2 key pair already exists for this Instaclustr account in every configured data centre region in the target AWS account (created by another RUNNING BYOC setup, or by this setup if already validated). Terraform users should pass create_key_pair = false when applying the template. When false, individual regions may still overlap the RUNNING accounts named in existingKeyPairProviderAccountNames; compare their data centre mappings and set create_key_pair = false only for overlapping regions. CloudFormation downloads set CreateKeyPair automatically per region.

status.description: Status of the BYOC provider account setup.

ByocAwsProviderAccountSetupV1.description: A resource representing a BYOC provider account setup record.

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

pciComplianceMode.description: Creates a PCI compliant cluster, see [PCI Compliance](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/pci-compliance/).

targetPrimaryCadence.description: Supporting Primary Cadence info for Multi region Cadence.

sharedProvisioning.description: Settings for SHARED provisioning. Must not be defined with STANDARD provisioning options. Can only use node sizes with prefix `CAD-SI`.

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

targetSecondaryCadence.description: Supporting Secondary Cadence info for Multi region Cadence.

cadenceVersion.description:
Version of Cadence to run on the cluster. Available versions:
  • `1.3.6`

standardProvisioning.description: Settings for STARDARD provisioning. Must not be defined with SHARED provisioning options. Can not use node sizes with prefix `CAD-SI`.

privateNetworkCluster.description: Creates the cluster with private network only, see [Private Network Clusters](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/private-network-clusters/).

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

id.description: ID of the cluster.

CadenceClusterV2.description: Definition of a managed Cadence cluster that can be provisioned in Instaclustr.

deletedNodes.description: List of deleted nodes in the data centre

awsSettings.description: AWS specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with GCP or Azure settings.
awsSettings.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

tagManagementEnabled.description: (Optional) Enable tag management for the data centre, allowing you to create, update and delete custom tags on the data centre via Instaclustr Terraform Provider v2, Cluster Management API or Management Console. Tag management is only available for RIYOA clusters and cannot be disabled once enabled. If not specified, the current value will remain unchanged.

currentOperations.description: Active operations in the data centre.

numberOfNodes.description: Total number of nodes in the Data Centre.

networks.description: All network CIDR blocks for this data centre, including the primary network and any expanded secondary CIDRs.

network.description: The private network address block for the Data Centre specified using CIDR address notation. The network must have a prefix length between `/16` and `/26` and must be part of a private address space.

tags.description: List of tags to apply to the Data Centre. Tags are metadata labels which allow you to identify, categorize and filter clusters. This can be useful for grouping together clusters into applications, environments, or any category that you require. Note: Tags will be returned sorted by key in alphabetical order regardless of input order. Terraform users: `tag` is not supported in terraform lifecycle `ignore_changes`.

zeroInboundAccess.description: Zero Inbound Access gateways eliminate the requirement for any public IP addresses in cluster deployment.

gcpSettings.description: GCP specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or Azure settings.

nodes.description: List of non-deleted nodes in the data centre

azureSettings.description: Azure specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or GCP settings.

name.description: A logical name for the data centre within a cluster. These names must be unique in the cluster.

id.description: ID of the Cluster Data Centre.

region.description: Region of the Data Centre. See the description for node size for a compatible Data Centre for a given node size.

privateLink.description: Create a PrivateLink enabled cluster, see [PrivateLink](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/privatelink/).

providerAccountName.description: For customers running in their own account. Your provider account can be found on the Create Cluster page on the Instaclustr Console, or the "Provider Account" property on any existing cluster. For customers provisioning on Instaclustr's cloud provider accounts, this property may be omitted.

dependencyCdcId.description: ID of the supporting Cluster's Cluster Data Centre

domainName.description: Exact Cadence domain name. It must start with a letter and may contain letters, numbers, periods, underscores, and hyphens. Cadence determines the supported maximum length.

requestsPerSecond.description: Requests per second for the domain.

CadenceDomainRateLimitSummaryV2.description: A request rate limit for one Cadence domain.

defaultRequestsPerSecond.description: Requests per second for all domains without a domain-specific limit. Written as the final unconstrained Cadence rule.

domainRateLimits.description: One cluster-wide request rate limit per Cadence domain. Supersedes the entire prior active rule set.

CadenceDomainRateLimitsUpdateV2.description: The complete frontend.globalDomainrps rule set for a Cadence cluster. At least one domain rate limit or a default request rate limit must be specified.

defaultRequestsPerSecond.description: Requests per second for all domains without a domain-specific limit. Written as the final unconstrained Cadence rule.

id.description: ID of the Cadence global domain request-rate-limits resource (the target cluster ID).

CadenceDomainRateLimitsV2.description: Domain request rate limits for a Cadence cluster.

defaultRequestsPerSecond.description: Requests per second for all domains without a domain-specific limit. Written as the final unconstrained Cadence rule.

domainRateLimits.description: One per-frontend-instance request rate limit per Cadence domain. Supersedes the entire prior active rule set.

CadenceFrontendDomainRateLimitsUpdateV2.description: The complete frontend.domainrps rule set for a Cadence cluster. At least one domain rate limit or a default request rate limit must be specified.

defaultRequestsPerSecond.description: Requests per second for all domains without a domain-specific limit. Written as the final unconstrained Cadence rule.

id.description: ID of the Cadence domain request-rate-limits resource (the target cluster ID).

CadenceFrontendDomainRateLimitsV2.description: Per-frontend-instance domain request rate limits for a Cadence cluster.

targetCassandraCdcId.description: UUID of a Data Centre of an Instaclustr managed Cassandra Cluster, to be used by Cadence. Must be in the same Instaclustr account.

targetKafkaCdcId.description: UUID of a Data Centre of an Instaclustr managed Kafka Cluster, to be used by Cadence. Must be in the same Instaclustr account.

targetOpenSearchCdcId.description: UUID of a Data Centre of an Instaclustr managed OpenSearch Cluster, to be used by Cadence. Must be in the same Instaclustr account.

archivalS3Uri.description: URI of S3 resource for Cadence Archival e.g. 's3://my-bucket'

archivalS3Region.description: Region of S3 resource for Cadence Archival e.g. 'us-east-1'

awsAccessKeyId.description: Access Key ID for IAM user with Archival bucket access

awsSecretAccessKey.description: Secret Access Key for IAM user with Archival bucket access

provisioningType.description: Provisioning Type used for the Cadence cluster. If SHARED is used, then the dependant clusters will be set to the Shared Infrastructure clusters.

advertisedHostName.description: Advertised HostName is required for PrivateLink.

cdcConfigs.description:
An optional list of Cluster Data Centres to determine their VPC in the restored cluster.

Data centres not included will default to being restored to a new VPC.

keyspaceTables.description: A comma separated list of keyspace/table names which follows the format \<keyspace\>.\<table1\>,\<keyspace\>.\<table2\>

pointInTime.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds since epoch or ISO formatted date and time (example - 2023-11-05T13:15:30Z). All backed up data will be restored for this point in time.

Defaults to the current date and time.

restoredClusterName.description:
The display name of the restored cluster.

By default, the restored cluster will be created with its current name appended with “restored” and the date & time it was requested to be restored.

clusterNetwork.description: The cluster network for this cluster to be restored to.

CassandraClusterRestoreV2.description: Definition of a Restore to be applied to a Cassandra cluster

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

pciComplianceMode.description: Creates a PCI compliant cluster, see [PCI Compliance](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/pci-compliance/).

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

defaultUserPassword.description: Password of the default user created for the Cassandra cluster.

privateNetworkCluster.description: Creates the cluster with private network only, see [Private Network Clusters](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/private-network-clusters/).

cassandraVersion.description:
Version of Cassandra to run on the cluster. Available versions:
  • `4.0.19`
  • `4.1.12`
  • `4.1.10`
  • `4.0.21`
  • `5.0.9`
  • `5.0.6`

luceneEnabled.description: Adds Apache Lucene to the Cassandra cluster.

passwordAndUserAuth.description: Enables Password Authentication and User Authorization.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

id.description: ID of the cluster.

CassandraClusterV2.description: Definition of a managed Cassandra cluster that can be provisioned in Instaclustr.

replicationFactor.description: Number of racks to use when allocating nodes.

pscNetwork.description: The private network address block for PSC subnets, specified as a CIDR. Prefix length must be between /12 and /22 and must be a private address space. If not provided, the next available network will be used.

deletedNodes.description: List of deleted nodes in the data centre

debezium.description: Adds the specified version of Debezium Connector Cassandra to the Cassandra cluster, as well as the Kafka Cluster Data Centre ID, Kafka VPC Type, and Kafka Topic Prefix.

currentOperations.description: Active operations in the data centre.

privateServiceConnectV2.description: Create a Private Service Connect enabled cluster.

numberOfNodes.description: Total number of nodes in the Data Centre. Includes only Cassandra nodes, other node types in the cluster such as shotover nodes are excluded from this count. Must be a multiple of `replicationFactor`.

networks.description: All network CIDR blocks for this data centre, including the primary network and any expanded secondary CIDRs.

network.description: The private network address block for the Data Centre specified using CIDR address notation. The network must have a prefix length between `/16` and `/26` and must be part of a private address space.

zeroInboundAccess.description: Zero Inbound Access gateways eliminate the requirement for any public IP addresses in cluster deployment.

id.description: ID of the Cluster Data Centre.

clusterDns.description: Enable cluster DNS for the data centre. When enabled, a DNS entry is created for this CDC pointing to cluster nodes, with additional addresses per node purpose. Incompatible with Private Link clusters. Cannot be disabled once enabled.

privateLink.description: Create a PrivateLink enabled cluster, see [PrivateLink](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/privatelink/).

continuousBackup.description: Enables commitlog backups and increases the frequency of the default snapshot backups.

awsSettings.description: AWS specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with GCP or Azure settings.
awsSettings.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

tagManagementEnabled.description: (Optional) Enable tag management for the data centre, allowing you to create, update and delete custom tags on the data centre via Instaclustr Terraform Provider v2, Cluster Management API or Management Console. Tag management is only available for RIYOA clusters and cannot be disabled once enabled. If not specified, the current value will remain unchanged.

clusterDnsZones.description: Cluster DNS hosted zones for this data centre: each entry is a DNS domain with the VPCs associated for private zone resolution.

shotoverProxy.description: Details of the Shotover Proxy nodes provisioned for Private Link.

customSubjectAlternativeNames.description: List of Subject Alternate Names FQDNs as per RFC 1035.  Used by the applications with self signed certificates in keystores of nodes in the datacenter.

privateIpBroadcastForDiscovery.description: Enables broadcast of private IPs for auto-discovery.

tags.description: List of tags to apply to the Data Centre. Tags are metadata labels which allow you to identify, categorize and filter clusters. This can be useful for grouping together clusters into applications, environments, or any category that you require. Note: Tags will be returned sorted by key in alphabetical order regardless of input order. Terraform users: `tag` is not supported in terraform lifecycle `ignore_changes`.

gcpSettings.description: GCP specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or Azure settings.

nodes.description: List of non-deleted nodes in the data centre

privateConnectivity.description: Configuration required for connecting to a PrivateLink or Private Service Connect enabled cluster.
privateConnectivity.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

azureSettings.description: Azure specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or GCP settings.

name.description: A logical name for the data centre within a cluster. These names must be unique in the cluster.

region.description: Region of the Data Centre. See the description for node size for a compatible Data Centre for a given node size.

providerAccountName.description: For customers running in their own account. Your provider account can be found on the Create Cluster page on the Instaclustr Console, or the "Provider Account" property on any existing cluster. For customers provisioning on Instaclustr's cloud provider accounts, this property may be omitted.

authnAuthz.description: Accepts true/false. Enables Password Authentication and User Authorization.

clientEncryption.description: Accepts true/false. Enables Client ⇄ Node Encryption.

usePrivateBroadcastRPCAddress.description: Enables broadcast of private IPs for auto-discovery.

luceneEnabled.description: Enables broadcast of private IPs for auto-discovery.

continuousBackupEnabled.description: Enables commitlog backups and increases the frequency of the default snapshot backups. This option replaces options.backupEnabled.

shotoverProxyNodeSize.description: Shotover Proxy Node Size. This option is applicable only for PrivateLink Cassandra Clusters

rack.description: The rack the endpoint is in

address.description: The ip address of the endpoint

endpointAddresses.description: Private Link / Private Service Connect endpoint addresses

CassandraPrivateServiceConnectRackInfoBy.description: GCP Private Service Connect Rack Information by Data Center

CassandraPrivateServiceConnectRackInfoV2.description: GCP Private Service Connect Rack Information

topCount.description: argument top count for top partitions

nodeId.description: Target node to execute top partitions

cdcId.description: Target cluster to execute top partitions

sampler.description: argument sampler for top partitions, 0: READS, 1: WRITES, 2: ALL

status.description: Current state of top partitions operation

CassandraTopPartitionsV2.description: Payload for top partitions against a given cluster node

cidr.description: Network CIDR in notation, for example 10.0.0.0/16.

primary.description: True when this entry is the data centre primary network.

status.description: Provisioning status of the network registration.

CdcNetworkDetailsV2.description: A network CIDR associated with the data centre (primary or expanded secondary).

CidrSetSchema.description: The subnets for the peering VPC, mutually exclusive with peerSubnet

endpointServiceName.description: The endpoint service name for the PrivateLink connection.

useAwsPrivateLink.description: Enable PrivateLink on the cluster, see [PrivateLink](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/privatelink/).

ClickHouseAwsPrivateLinkSettingsV2.description: Settings required for AWS Private Link to be enabled on a cluster.

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

defaultUserPassword.description: Password of the default user created for the ClickHouse cluster.

privateNetworkCluster.description: Creates the cluster with private network only, see [Private Network Clusters](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/private-network-clusters/).

clickhouseVersion.description:
Version of ClickHouse to run on the cluster. Available versions:
  • `26.3.29`
  • `26.8.2`

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

id.description: ID of the cluster.

ClickHouseClusterV2.description: Definition of a managed ClickHouse cluster that can be provisioned in Instaclustr.

value.description: Override value for the configuration property.

id.description: ID of the cluster's configuration. This should be of the form: 'cfg-<cluster uuid>'.

deletedNodes.description: List of deleted nodes in the data centre

currentOperations.description: Active operations in the data centre.

networks.description: All network CIDR blocks for this data centre, including the primary network and any expanded secondary CIDRs.

dedicatedClickHouseKeeper.description: Provision additional dedicated nodes for ClickHouse Keeper to run on. ClickHouse Keeper will be co-located with ClickHouse Server if this is not provided.

network.description: The private network address block for the Data Centre specified using CIDR address notation. The network must have a prefix length between `/16` and `/26` and must be part of a private address space.

zeroInboundAccess.description: Zero Inbound Access gateways eliminate the requirement for any public IP addresses in cluster deployment.

dataCentreCustomName.description:
Optional. Assign a custom name for the data centre when creating a cluster with a single data centre.

For clusters with multiple data centres use dataCentres.name instead

cdcConfigs.description:
An optional list of Cluster Data Centres to determine their VPC in the restored cluster.

Data centres not included will default to being restored to a new VPC.

pointInTime.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds since epoch or ISO formatted date and time (example - 2023-11-05T13:15:30Z). All backed up data will be restored for this point in time.

Defaults to the current date and time.

restoredClusterName.description:
The display name of the restored cluster.

By default, the restored cluster will be created with its current name appended with “restored” and the date & time it was requested to be restored.

ClusterRestoreV2.description: Definition of a Restore to be applied to a cluster

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

ClusterSettingsUpdateV2.description: The non-application specific settings of the cluster

relatedClusterIds.description: IDs of all clusters included in this suspend or resume, including the originating cluster. For a standalone cluster this contains only the originating ID.

clusterStatus.description: Transitional cluster status after the request was accepted (SUSPENDING after suspend, RESUMING after resume). Poll cluster details until the status reaches SUSPENDED or RUNNING.

ClusterSuspendResumeStatusV2.description: Accepted response after starting cluster suspend or resume. Confirms the cluster is suspending or resuming. Includes IDs of related application-group and dependent clusters when those are expanded automatically. No workflow/job detail is returned.

id.description: ID of the cluster.

ClusterWaiterV2.description: Definition of a waiter resource so Terraform can wait for the provisioning of the given cluster to complete. **NOTE** - deleting this resource is an empty operation and will not delete the original cluster.

end.description: Timestamp of when the event was completed. Can be null.

CommonClusterRestoreModeEnumV2.description:
Determines the target VPC for restored cluster. Accepted values are:
  • NEW_VPC - restores the cluster to a new VPC.
  • SAME_VPC - restores the cluster to the same VPC as the original cluster, for customers running in their own account.
    • AWS - restore to a new Cidr within the CDC's network
    • GCP - For customer-managed network, if the source cluster specifies a host project, it will be restored to that project. If the source cluster specifies a custom subnet, it will be restored to that custom subnet. If nothing is specified, it will restore to a new Cidr within the CDC network.
    • Azure - currently not supported.
  • CUSTOM_VPC - restores the cluster to a custom VPC for customers running in their own account. Customers need to specify the customVpcSettings including network and vpcId.
    • AWS - restores the cluster to the network Cidr and vpc specified by the customer
    • GCP - For customer-managed network, if the vpcId field contains the projects/ pattern, it will be restored to that project. If the vpcId field contains the subnetworks/ pattern, it will be restored to that custom subnet. If nothing is specified, it will restore to a new Cidr within the CDC network.
    • Azure - restores the cluster to the network Cidr and VNet specified by the customer.
    CUSTOM_VPC and SAME_VPC options are available only for customers running in their own account.

pointInTime.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds since epoch or ISO formatted date and time (example - 2023-11-05T13:15:30Z). All backed up data will be restored for this point in time.

Defaults to the current date and time.

deletedNodes.description: List of deleted nodes in the data centre

awsSettings.description: AWS specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with GCP or Azure settings.
awsSettings.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

tagManagementEnabled.description: (Optional) Enable tag management for the data centre, allowing you to create, update and delete custom tags on the data centre via Instaclustr Terraform Provider v2, Cluster Management API or Management Console. Tag management is only available for RIYOA clusters and cannot be disabled once enabled. If not specified, the current value will remain unchanged.

currentOperations.description: Active operations in the data centre.

numberOfNodes.description: Total number of Kafka brokers in the Data Centre. Must be a multiple of `defaultReplicationFactor`.

additionalListeners.description: The additional listeners to create for a kafka cluster along with the default one.

networks.description: All network CIDR blocks for this data centre, including the primary network and any expanded secondary CIDRs.

customSubjectAlternativeNames.description: List of Subject Alternative Names FQDNs as per RFC 1035.  Used by the applications with self signed certificates in keystores of nodes in the datacenter. NOTE: No private link cluster support.

network.description: The private network address block for the Data Centre specified using CIDR address notation. The network must have a prefix length between `/16` and `/26` and must be part of a private address space.

tags.description: List of tags to apply to the Data Centre. Tags are metadata labels which allow you to identify, categorize and filter clusters. This can be useful for grouping together clusters into applications, environments, or any category that you require. nodes.description: List of non-deleted nodes in the data centre

azureSettings.description: Azure specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or GCP settings.

name.description: A logical name for the data centre within a cluster. These names must be unique in the cluster.

id.description: ID of the Cluster Data Centre.

region.description: Region of the Data Centre. See the description for node size for a compatible Data Centre for a given node size.

privateLink.description: Create a PrivateLink enabled cluster, see [PrivateLink](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/privatelink/).
privateLink.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

providerAccountName.description: For customers running in their own account. Your provider account can be found on the Create Cluster page on the Instaclustr Console, or the "Provider Account" property on any existing cluster. For customers provisioning on Instaclustr's cloud provider accounts, this property may be omitted.

customListeners.description: The custom listeners to create for a kafka cluster along with the default one.

deletedNodes.description: List of deleted nodes in the data centre

currentOperations.description: Active operations in the data centre.

numberOfNodes.description: Total number of Kafka brokers in the Data Centre. Must be a multiple of `defaultReplicationFactor`.

networks.description: All network CIDR blocks for this data centre, including the primary network and any expanded secondary CIDRs.

network.description: The private network address block for the Data Centre specified using CIDR address notation. The network must have a prefix length between `/16` and `/26` and must be part of a private address space.

zeroInboundAccess.description: Zero Inbound Access gateways eliminate the requirement for any public IP addresses in cluster deployment.

id.description: ID of the Cluster Data Centre.

clusterDns.description: Enable cluster DNS for the data centre. When enabled, a DNS entry is created for this CDC pointing to cluster nodes, with additional addresses per node purpose. Incompatible with Private Link clusters. Cannot be disabled once enabled.

awsSettings.description: AWS specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with GCP or Azure settings.
awsSettings.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

tagManagementEnabled.description: (Optional) Enable tag management for the data centre, allowing you to create, update and delete custom tags on the data centre via Instaclustr Terraform Provider v2, Cluster Management API or Management Console. Tag management is only available for RIYOA clusters and cannot be disabled once enabled. If not specified, the current value will remain unchanged.

clusterDnsZones.description: Cluster DNS hosted zones for this data centre: each entry is a DNS domain with the VPCs associated for private zone resolution.

additionalListeners.description: The additional listeners to create for a kafka cluster along with the default one.

customSubjectAlternativeNames.description: List of Subject Alternate Names FQDNs as per RFC 1035.  Used by the applications with self signed certificates in keystores of nodes in the datacenter.

tags.description: List of tags to apply to the Data Centre. Tags are metadata labels which allow you to identify, categorize and filter clusters. This can be useful for grouping together clusters into applications, environments, or any category that you require. Note: Tags will be returned sorted by key in alphabetical order regardless of input order. Terraform users: `tag` is not supported in terraform lifecycle `ignore_changes`.

gcpSettings.description: GCP specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or Azure settings.

nodes.description: List of non-deleted nodes in the data centre

privateConnectivity.description: Create a PrivateLink/Private Service Connect enabled cluster, see [PrivateLink](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/privatelink/).
privateConnectivity.x-insta-comment: due to a bug with the terraform provider openapi plugin this has to be a list instead of a nested object. Also has to be computed because terraform defaults lists to empty arrays when skipped, whereas the API returns null

azureSettings.description: Azure specific settings for the Data Centre. Cannot be provided with AWS or GCP settings.

name.description: A logical name for the data centre within a cluster. These names must be unique in the cluster.

region.description: Region of the Data Centre. See the description for node size for a compatible Data Centre for a given node size.

providerAccountName.description: For customers running in their own account. Your provider account can be found on the Create Cluster page on the Instaclustr Console, or the "Provider Account" property on any existing cluster. For customers provisioning on Instaclustr's cloud provider accounts, this property may be omitted.

controllerNodeSize.description: Size of the nodes provisioned as dedicated KRaft Controller nodes.
Size of the nodes provisioned as dedicated KRaftController nodes.

pointInTime.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds since epoch or ISO formatted date and time (example - 2023-11-05T13:15:30Z). All backed up data will be restored for this point in time.

Defaults to the current date and time.
pointInTime.x-insta-comment: No force-new since this is expected to be used in Terraform and we expect customers would eventually delete their old cluster.

indexNames.description:
A comma separated list of index names which follows the format `index1,index2`

If provided, only data for the specified indices will be restored, for the point in time. If not provided, all indices will be restored for the point in time.
indexNames.x-insta-comment: No force-new since this is expected to be used in Terraform and we expect customers would eventually delete their old cluster.

clusterId.description: ID of the target cluster used for the restore operation.
clusterId.x-insta-comment: No force-new since this is expected to be used in Terraform and we expect customers would eventually delete their old cluster.

cdcConfigs.description:
An optional list of Cluster Data Centres to determine their VPC in the restored cluster.

Data centres not included will default to being restored to a new VPC.

pointInTime.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds since epoch or ISO formatted date and time (example - 2023-11-05T13:15:30Z). All backed up data will be restored for this point in time.

Defaults to the current date and time.

restoredClusterName.description:
The display name of the restored cluster.

By default, the restored cluster will be created with its current name appended with “restored” and the date & time it was requested to be restored.

indexNames.description:
A comma separated list of index names which follows the format `index1,index2`

If provided, only data for the specified indices will be restored, for the point in time. If not provided, all indices will be restored for the point in time.

clusterNetwork.description: The cluster network for this cluster to be restored to.

OpenSearchClusterRestoreV2.description: Definition of a Restore to be applied to a Opensearch cluster

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

vectorIndexBuilder.description: Remote Vector Index Builder settings. Change nodeSize to resize the existing dedicated GPU host. Adding a Vector Index Builder to an existing cluster is not supported.

publicEndpoint.description: Public endpoint to connect clients to the cluster. Not applicable to Private IP only clusters.

opensearchVersion.description:
Version of OpenSearch to run on the cluster. Must be provided if `opensearchMajorVersion` is not provided. Available versions:
  • `2.19.5`
  • `2.19.6`
  • `3.5.0`
  • `3.6.0`

leaderClusterAccount.description: The leader cluster account ID for a Cross Cluster Replication enabled follower cluster. This requires crossClusterReplicationPlugin to be set to true.

searchableSnapshots.description: Enable searchable snapshots. Available only for OpenSearch versions 2.7.0 or higher.

description.example: Cluster managed by the integration team.

privateEndpoint.description: Private endpoint to connect clients to the cluster.

vectorIndexBuilder.description: Remote Vector Index Builder settings. When provided, a dedicated GPU host is provisioned.

ingestNodesLoadBalancerConnectionUrl.description: URL of the Ingest Nodes specific Network Load Balancer if a load balancer is enabled for the cluster. Balances request loads against nodes with the ingest role. Recommended for clusters with dedicated ingest nodes.

notificationsPlugin.description: Enables notifications plugin. For OpenSearch 2.x and later, if you want to enable this plugin you must also enable the Alerting plugin.

nodeTypeAttributesEnabled.description: Enable managed node_type attributes. Requires the OPENSEARCH_NODE_TYPE_ATTRIBUTES account feature. Exactly one data-role node per rack is assigned node_type=metadata and all remaining data-role nodes are assigned node_type=data.

leaderClusterId.description: Specifies the leader cluster ID for a Cross Cluster Replication enabled follower cluster. This requires crossClusterReplicationPlugin to be set to true. Not defining this will make the cluster a leader cluster if crossClusterReplicationPlugin is set to true.

privateNetworkCluster.description: Creates the cluster with private network only, see [Private Network Clusters](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/private-network-clusters/).

restoreSettings.description: Triggers a restore operation when provided during cluster creation. Contains the settings for the restore request.

resizeSettings.description: Settings to determine how resize requests will be performed for the cluster.

id.description: ID of the cluster.

pciComplianceMode.description: Creates a PCI compliant cluster, see [PCI Compliance](https://www.instaclustr.com/support/documentation/useful-information/pci-compliance/).

anonymousAuthEnabled.description: Enable anonymous authentication. Allows unauthenticated requests with restricted  permissions. Requires Private Network Cluster. Not available when PCI compliance mode is enabled.

opensearchMajorVersion.description: Major version of OpenSearch to run on the cluster. Must be provided if `opensearchVersion` is not provided.

enableBidirectionalReplication.description: When true, provisions the new follower with bi-directional OpenSearch cross-cluster replication against the specified leader. Requires `leaderClusterId` and `crossClusterReplicationPlugin` to be set to true. The account must have the OpenSearch bi-directional CCR feature enabled. On GET, true when this cluster is a bi-directional follower of its leader.

defaultUserPassword.description: Password of the default user created for the OpenSearch cluster.

loadBalancerConnectionUrl.description: URL of the Network Load Balancer if a load balancer is enabled for the cluster. Balances request loads against all nodes in the cluster except for ingest nodes.

defaultUsername.description: Username of the default user created for the OpenSearch cluster.

clusterManagerNodes.description: List of cluster managers node settings

portal26Plugin.description: Whether or not the Portal26 plugin is enabled for this cluster.

alertingPlugin.description: Enables alerting plugin. For OpenSearch 2.x and later, if you want to enable this plugin you must also enable the Notifications plugin.
